Competency: Manage role based access control (RBAC)
Challenge: Bind the settlement team to a Role in the settlement namespace and remove the cluster-admin binding left on them.
Essence: A grant is a Role in one namespace. cluster-admin is the wrong grant.

Competency: Prepare underlying infrastructure for installing a Kubernetes cluster
Challenge: On a fresh machine, turn swap off, load the modules, open the API ports, and leave containerd running. kubeadm is the next lab.
Essence: The machine is ready before kubeadm runs. The cluster does not exist yet.

Competency: Create and manage Kubernetes clusters using kubeadm
Challenge: kubeadm init the control plane and kubeadm join the worker. kubectl lists both nodes Ready.
Essence: kubeadm init builds the control plane. kubeadm join adds a worker.

Competency: Manage the lifecycle of Kubernetes clusters
Challenge: Upgrade the control plane with kubeadm and then the worker. order-processor stays Ready on the worker through the drain. Take an etcd snapshot before the upgrade.
Essence: Lifecycle is a kubeadm upgrade one node at a time and an etcd snapshot you can restore.

Competency: Implement and configure a highly-available control plane
Challenge: Three control plane nodes share a stacked etcd. Stop one. The API still answers and payment-handler stays Running.
Essence: More than one control plane. One of them can die and the API stays up.

Competency: Use Helm and Kustomize to install cluster components
Challenge: Install metrics-server with Helm and the ingress controller with Kustomize. Do not apply their raw manifests by hand.
Essence: Cluster components are installed as a chart and a kustomization.

Competency: Understand extension interfaces (CNI, CSI, CRI, etc.)
Challenge: Pods stay ContainerCreating with no IP. Install the CNI. Record the CRI the node is using and the CSI behind the StorageClass.
Essence: CNI gives the pod an IP. CRI runs the container. CSI provisions the disk.

Competency: Understand CRDs, install and configure operators
Challenge: Install the operator. Create one custom resource. The operator creates the Deployment. Deleting the resource deletes the Deployment.
Essence: A CRD adds an API. An operator is the controller that acts on it.

Competency: Understand application deployments and how to perform rolling update and rollbacks
Challenge: Roll order-processor to the new image. That image crashloops. Roll the Deployment back. The running image is the previous one.
Essence: A Deployment rolls forward and rolls back. The ReplicaSet history is the previous image.

Competency: Use ConfigMaps and Secrets to configure applications
Challenge: payment-handler reads its config from a ConfigMap and its key from a Secret. The values are not in the image.
Essence: Config is a ConfigMap. A credential is a Secret. Neither is baked into the image.

Competency: Configure workload autoscaling
Challenge: Put an HPA on notification-service. Under load the replica count rises and stops at the max in the ticket.
Essence: An HPA changes the replica count from measured CPU. metrics-server is what it reads.

Competency: Understand the primitives used to create robust, self-healing, application deployments
Challenge: order-processor has 3 replicas, a liveness probe, and a readiness probe. A crashed container is restarted. An unready pod leaves the Service. The Deployment brings the count back.
Essence: Replicas plus probes. The Deployment replaces a pod. A human does not.

Competency: Configure Pod admission and scheduling (limits, node affinity, etc.)
Challenge: A LimitRange fills default requests. payment-handler tolerates the pci taint and has a node affinity for node-b. A pod over the quota stays Pending.
Essence: Admission fills limits and rejects what does not fit. Affinity and taints choose the node.

Competency: Understand connectivity between Pods
Challenge: order-processor on node-a reaches payment-handler by pod IP on node-b. The Service is not the path under test.
Essence: Every pod has an IP. Pods on different nodes reach each other by that IP.

Competency: Define and enforce Network Policies
Challenge: The payments namespace denies all ingress. Only order-processor may call payment-handler on its port. A pod in notifications is refused.
Essence: A NetworkPolicy is the allowed path. Everything else in that namespace is refused.

Competency: Use ClusterIP NodePort LoadBalancer service types and endpoints
Challenge: payment-handler is a ClusterIP. QA uses a NodePort. The partner entry is a LoadBalancer. A process with no selector is reached through an Endpoints object.
Essence: ClusterIP NodePort and LoadBalancer are three ways in. Endpoints are the pods a Service sends to.

Competency: Use the Gateway API to manage Ingress traffic
Challenge: An HTTPRoute on the lab gateway sends /pay to payment-handler and /orders to order-processor.
Essence: A Gateway and an HTTPRoute are the path from outside the cluster to a Service.

Competency: Know how to use Ingress controllers and Ingress resources
Challenge: Install the ingress controller. An Ingress for the host in the ticket reaches order-processor.
Essence: An Ingress does nothing until its controller is running. The resource is the host and the path.

Competency: Understand and use CoreDNS
Challenge: Service names fail. The CoreDNS ConfigMap has the wrong cluster domain. Put cluster.local back. A lookup of payment-handler.payments.svc.cluster.local succeeds.
Essence: CoreDNS is how a Service name becomes an IP. The cluster domain is a CoreDNS setting.

Competency: Implement storage classes and dynamic volume provisioning
Challenge: A PVC that names the company StorageClass binds with no one creating a PV. The provisioner creates the volume.
Essence: A StorageClass is the provisioner. The claim creates the volume.

Competency: Configure volume types access modes and reclaim policies
Challenge: The archive volume is ReadWriteOnce and its reclaim policy is Retain. Deleting the claim leaves the PV and the data.
Essence: Access mode is who can mount it. Reclaim is what happens to the disk when the claim is deleted.

Competency: Manage persistent volumes and persistent volume claims
Challenge: Create the PV. The claim binds to it. The pod mounts it and writes a file. A new pod for the same claim still sees the file.
Essence: A PV is the disk. A PVC is the request. The pod sees a mount.

Competency: Troubleshoot clusters and nodes
Challenge: node-b is NotReady and the API on the other node still answers. Bring node-b back to Ready. Do not delete the Node.
Essence: A NotReady node is the kubelet the disk or the condition. The node object stays.

Competency: Troubleshoot cluster components
Challenge: New pods stay Pending. The scheduler static pod is crashlooping on a bad flag in its manifest. Fix the manifest. Pods that are already running keep running.
Essence: Control plane components are static pods. The manifest on the node is the source. kubectl describe and the log name the bad flag.

Competency: Monitor cluster and application resource usage
Challenge: kubectl top shows payment-handler at its memory limit and restarting. Raise that limit to the value in the ticket. The other Deployments stay as they are.
Essence: metrics-server is how the cluster shows CPU and memory. A limit that is too small restarts the container.

Competency: Manage and evaluate container output streams
Challenge: notification-service is crashlooping. The reason is in the previous container log. The sidecar is a different stream.
Essence: stdout and stderr are the container log. The previous container keeps the last crash. Each container in the pod has its own stream.

Competency: Troubleshoot services and networking
Challenge: payment-handler is Running and its Service exists. The Service has no Endpoints because the selector does not match. Fix the selector.
Essence: A Service with no Endpoints has a selector that matches nothing. DNS and NetworkPolicy are the other two breaks on this line.

Competency: Apply the settlement request
Challenge: A request file for settlement is in the ticket. The checker creates the namespace to the lab 01 spec and does not touch the namespaces already live.
Essence: Namespace changes go through a tool that knows the company rules.

Competency: Refuse the bad template
Challenge: The same checker is handed cluster-admin and no quota. It refuses and leaves the cluster unchanged.
Essence: The tool fails closed. A bad request creates nothing.

Competency: Node report
Challenge: Ship a command that prints every worker that is not Ready and exits non-zero when any worker is down.
Essence: The on-call check for nodes is a tool.

Competency: Pending pod report
Challenge: Ship a report that lists Pending pods and the reason. A cluster with nothing Pending prints nothing and exits clean.
Essence: The on-call check for unschedulable work is the same kind of tool.

Competency: Access from the team template
Challenge: Apply the template. deploy-bot may update Deployments in orders. The settlement team may work in settlement only. A delete of a payments Secret as deploy-bot is denied.
Essence: Access is a template.

Competency: Quota the replay namespace
Challenge: The replay namespace is creating pods with no limit and starving the node. Put a ResourceQuota on that namespace only.
Essence: A quota is how the platform stops one team from crowding the node.

Competency: Detect namespace drift
Challenge: The desired file says settlement has a pod quota of 10 and a default memory limit. The cluster was left without the limit. The tool prints the difference and does not change anything.
Essence: Seeing drift and fixing drift are separate.

Competency: Reconcile settlement
Challenge: Same drift as the previous lab. The tool applies the file and waits until the quota and the default limit are in place.
Essence: The tool can repair a namespace back to the file.

Competency: Drain helper
Challenge: A command cordons and drains one worker and leaves payment-handler serving on the other. It refuses the control-plane node as a target.
Essence: A drain is a tool with the same safety rules as the admin labs.

Competency: Namespace request API
Challenge: A small local API other teams call to open a namespace. It uses the same rules as the bad-template lab. A bad body is rejected. A good body creates the namespace.
Essence: Other teams ask for a namespace through the API.
